meta.title: Errors and Experimentation
meta.subtitle: Part 4: Learning Through Mistakes and Exploration
meta.description: Introduction to common errors in Python and basic experimentation strategies.

body.markdown: This is the fourth part of the `Jump In` guide. Here, we focus on **errors** and **experimentation**. Errors are a normal part of learning and programming. Consider them hints that something needs adjusting, not failures. Experimentation is about testing your ideas safely with small, simple steps.
Python errors usually come with a message that describes what went wrong. Below are the most common types beginners see:
A `SyntaxError` happens when Python doesn't understand the code structure (missing a parenthesis, colon, etc.).
A `NameError` occurs when you try to use something that hasn't been defined yet.
`TypeError` means the wrong type of object was used. `ValueError` means the type was right but the value didn't make sense.
`IndexError` means you asked for a position that doesn't exist.
`FileNotFoundError` and `PermissionError` happen when files or paths don't exist or can't be accessed. Relative vs. absolute paths, and read/write permissions, can all matter here.

body.title: Big Picture Errors
body.text:
Sometimes errors come from bigger issues: the Python version you're using, missing packages, or environment setup. This browser based tutorial should avoid any of those for now.

But be aware, those errors can cause lots of headaches.

Debugging is most effective when structured, check out [On the Shoulders of Giants]({{{shoulders-of-giants}}}) for more general tips.

body.markdown:
Experimentation means testing your ideas step by step.
Debugging works a lot like science. Instead of guessing randomly, you can treat each step as a test:

- **Form a hypothesis**: “Maybe the list is empty.”

- **Test it**: `print(len(my_list))`

- **Observe**: Check if the result matches your idea.

- **Revise**: If not, try a new explanation.

body.content:
total = 5 + 7
print("Total is:", total)
total = 57
print("Total is:", total)

body.markdown: Use `#` to comment out lines temporarily. Make one change at a time and re-run to see the effect.

body.content:
# Swap the commented section
message = "Hello"
print(message)

# numbers = [10, 20, 30]
# print(numbers[2])

body.title: Use f-Strings for Context Printing
body.text: Instead of guessing what a printed value means, f-strings let you add context directly in the output. They are one of the easiest ways to add clarity to print statements and much more.

body.content:
x = 42
print(f"The value of x is {x}")

name = "Alice"
age = 30
print(f"Name: {name}, Age: {age}")

body.markdown:
- Errors are hints, not failures.
- Experiment with simple tools (`type()`, `print()`, `len()`).
- More advanced error topics like environments, packages, and permissions are covered elsewhere.
